resources.string: Double-press a volume button to turn the torch on. Double-press it again to turn it off.
Accessibility setting: off. The app needs it to see volume button presses.
Android only lets an app see volume button presses if you turn it on in the accessibility settings. Every app that reacts to hardware buttons needs this.

string-array.name: setup_promises
string-array.item: It only reacts to the volume button you choose. Every other key goes straight back to Android, untouched.
It doesn’t read your screen, your notifications or what you type.
It keeps nothing but its own settings, and it has no internet permission, so it can’t go online.
You can switch it off at any time, in this app or in Android’s settings.
It’s open source, so anyone can check all of this.

resources.string: Android will ask whether to give the app full control of your device. It shows that same warning for every accessibility app, because some of them could do a lot. Simple Torch Launcher only asks Android for key presses.

string-array.name: setup_steps
string-array.item: Find Simple Torch Launcher. It’s often under “Downloaded apps” or “Installed apps”.
Turn it on, then tap Allow.

resources.string: Try it now: double-press volume up.
Try it now: double-press volume down.
It works! Double-press again to turn the torch off.
Torch off. That’s all there is to it.

Android blocks this for some apps installed outside an app store. Open App info, tap ⋮ in the top corner and choose “Allow restricted settings”. Then turn Simple Torch Launcher on in the accessibility settings again.
No torch found on this device
Single presses still change the volume, after a short delay.
Also work when the screen is off
Experimental. Works on many phones but not all, and not while music or other audio is playing.
This app is free. No ads, no tracking, no in-app purchases, and no internet access.
Free and open-source software, released under the MIT License.

Lets you double-press a volume button to turn the torch on and off.\n\nSimple Torch Launcher only reacts to volume button presses and ignores every other key. It doesn’t read your screen, keeps nothing but its own settings, and has no internet access.
